title: Zelda Ocarina of Time remake: Switch 2's fastest seller
description: The Zelda Ocarina of Time remake sold over 5.2 million copies in four days, Nintendo says, making it the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far.

body.text: The Zelda Ocarina of Time remake has become the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, according to Eurogamer, which reports that Nintendo moved more than 5.2 million copies in just four days. For Indian gamers watching where console gaming is heading, it is a loud signal that nostalgia still sells in huge numbers.
Zelda Ocarina of Time remake sales: what we know
Nintendo revealed the figure in a press release, as reported by Eurogamer. The headline number is 5.2 million copies sold across the first four days on shelves and storefronts.
That is all the source gives us. There is no breakdown by region, no revenue figure and no split between physical and digital copies, so we cannot say how the game performed in any single market.
The fine print on the record
Nintendo was specific about the claim. The record applies only to games published by Nintendo itself, not to every title released on the console.

Eurogamer points out that Nintendo's own games are the most popular on Switch 2, so the remake probably holds the title across the whole library as well. That is Eurogamer's reading, not something Nintendo stated.
Great reviews and a hardware bump
The sales come after a warm critical reception. Eurogamer's Christian Donlan gave the game five stars in the outlet's review and praised the remake for its smart tweaks and judgement.

Eurogamer also says it has already seen a jump in Switch 2 sales in the US because of the game's release. The outlet added a dig about the decision to launch in November, close to GTA 6, and suggested the timing has worked out fine for Nintendo so far.

items: More than 5.2 million copies sold in four days, per Nintendo's press release
Record covers Nintendo-published Switch 2 games only
A reported lift in US Switch 2 sales, according to Eurogamer

body.text: Eurogamer raises an obvious question: if a nostalgia-driven remake can do this, will Nintendo return to other beloved older Zelda games, or to other classic franchises? The outlet also wonders which Zelda titles have similar pull and have not yet been remade or remastered in some form.
To be clear, this is speculation from the publication. Nintendo has not announced any further remakes in the material we have seen.

Keep an eye out for updated sales figures as the game moves beyond its first week, and for any sign from Nintendo about its next remake or remaster. Whether the Switch 2 sales bump holds beyond the US is another thing to follow. If you are starting the game yourself, Eurogamer has a full set of Ocarina of Time guides to help you through it.
